problems.stem: In a three-turn scenario dialogue, which turn does the job of NARROW?
options: The turn that pastes the scenario and names the audience.
The turn that says 'Keep it under 90 seconds to read aloud; no jargon.'
The turn that asks 'What if the student already feels behind?'
The turn that copies the whole AI reply into the artifact.
problems.explanation: NARROW adds the constraint (length, tone). Pasting the scenario is SET CONTEXT; the 'what if' is STRESS-TEST.

problems.stem: A scenario reads only: 'A new student joined late. Draft what I say.' What constraint is missing that the model needs?
options: Audience, length, and tone (for example: nervous new student, under 90 seconds, no jargon).
The student's full name and ID number.
A request to make the answer longer.
problems.explanation: A scenario without constraints lets the model guess. Audience, length, and tone make the output usable.

problems.stem: Turn 3 returns two reassurance lines that say nearly the same thing. What is the strongest move for the saved artifact?
options: Keep both lines so the artifact is longer.
Keep one line and log that you cut the duplicate and why.
Delete the whole transcript and start over in one prompt.
Ask the AI to add a third reassurance line.
problems.explanation: Selecting one line and logging the cut makes your judgment part of the evidence; keeping both adds no information.

problems.stem: Why label each turn (SET CONTEXT, NARROW, STRESS-TEST) instead of writing one long prompt?
options: Labels make the prompt look more professional.
Labels let a reader see which turn caused which change in the output.
Labels force the AI to answer faster.
Labels are required by every AI tool.
problems.explanation: Labeled turns make the cause of each change traceable; one giant prompt hides which instruction did the work.
